scope: Dated upstream Linux capability and package observations. Each row carries its own review date and Assbox qualification status.

rows.browser: Documented browser actions in the Linux preview.
rows.desktop: Other desktop-app control is not yet supported in the reviewed release entry.
rows.scope: Native product on its documented Linux distributions; NixOS and exact client/policy still require qualification.
rows.implementation: Keep kiosk browser consent separate from local Work/Codex execution. No Xvfb workaround is advertised as enabling native screen control.

rows.browser: Built-in browser rollout includes Linux beta; account/rollout dependent.
rows.desktop: Reviewed native screen-control support lists macOS/Windows, not Linux.
rows.scope: Native Desktop browser bridge can be needed even when Cowork runs in the cloud; it must remain open/online.
rows.implementation: Qualify private browser state and selected local authority. Do not equate cloud Cowork with a remote browser or import personal cookies automatically.

rows.browser: Separate browser integrations are outside this native screen-control feature.
rows.desktop: Not supported on Linux by the reviewed CLI documentation; interactive macOS preview.
rows.scope: Native CLI feature, not Claude models used through OpenClaw/Hermes/OMP or another Linux-capable tool.
rows.implementation: Do not present a Linux virtual display as enabling this feature. A separately selected harness needs separate authentication, tools and evidence.

rows.desktop: Documented Linux X11 capture/input; headless TigerVNC/XFCE path.
rows.scope: Explicit computer-use opt-in; desktop sharing is separate. Agent loop/tool placement follows the self-hosted contract.
rows.implementation: Use pinned cursor-agent, required packages and provider-owned display lifecycle; scrub inherited DISPLAY and qualify viewer/cleanup behavior.

rows.desktop: Labs/opt-in Linux managed desktop and separately enabled computer tool.
rows.scope: TigerVNC/XFCE with private D-Bus; enabling a Desktop panel is not enabling CUA.
rows.implementation: Pin helper dependencies and require separate tool consent. Reject unrelated RFB listener selection; keep human viewing and active tool control distinct.

rows.path: Hermes browser / Cua Driver / Bot Screen
rows.browser: Documented local and cloud backends; inspect any local sidecar behavior.
rows.desktop: Documented Linux X11/Wayland paths with display, AT-SPI and capture prerequisites.
rows.scope: Current upstream feature docs; exact Hermes/Cua pin required. Native Wayland is opt-in, with documented capture/XWayland caveats. Bot Screen is provider-owned headless Xfce/TigerVNC.
rows.implementation: Prefer a qualified upstream Bot Screen when included in the pin; otherwise qualify the selected existing-display path. Preserve private egress and do not infer same-UID isolation.

rows.path: OMP 18.8.3 computer prelude and selected Nix recipe
rows.browser: Versioned documentation describes a separate browser prelude. The selected runtime and helper require their own test.
rows.desktop: Versioned documentation describes Linux X11 capture/input and conditional Wayland capture. The computer prelude starts disabled.
rows.scope: Assbox selects OMP 18.8.3 from recipe d6e0728e. Its Linux Cargo build requests wayland-pipewire, and a later N-API step can run before packaging. Upstream release binaries omit the Wayland capture feature. The selected addon and compositor behavior still need evidence.
rows.implementation: Inspect the actual installed addon and qualify permissions and capabilities on each display backend. Keep computer use off until selected and record X11 and Wayland results independently.
